title: Technique rules (techniques/<id>/technique.yaml)
description: Machine-readable rules for one testing technique: when to adopt, defer or reject it, checks to run first, and what to use instead. The technique decision tool reads these to mark each technique for a repo. Words follow GLOSSARY.md.

maturityLevel.description: A test maturity level (ADR-003): 0 builds reliably; 1 runs on its own; 2 current behaviour recorded; 3 checked against requirements; 4 tests proven to catch bugs; 5 checked in production.

id.description: Folder name; used in tt:technique/<id> labels and in decisions: entries.

reject_or_defer_when.description: Any one rules the technique out (reject) or postpones it until another track meets it (defer).

done_by.description: tool: an automated check. person: needs someone's sign-off.

fallback.description: What to use instead if rejected. A technique id where one exists, otherwise plain words.

workstream.description: The workstream whose issues this technique's work goes into. Roughly in this order: make it run on its own, fix flaky tests, record current behaviour, make code testable, test against requirements, strengthen tests, check in production.

test_stand_in_approach.description: Only for techniques in the make-it-run-on-its-own workstream: which test stand-in approach this technique implements.

evidence_for_maturity_levels.description: Which test maturity levels a repo can claim on the strength of tests produced by this technique. Example: Testcontainers tests can count towards levels 1 to 3; mutation testing is the evidence for level 4.

application_types.description: Application types whose testing guides adopt this by default. For information only; the testing guides are authoritative.

references.description: Anchors in docs/REFERENCES.md that give the background for this technique.
